Folks — I grabbed the control plane and agent side logs. Quick summary of what I see:

- At 08:50:12 we observe a spike in SYN-ACK retries on connections to controlplane-01 (IP masked in logs).
- TLS handshakes reported 'no shared cipher' on ~30% of failed attempts, while the rest show 'timeout during server hello'.
- The control plane nodes that were on the new build had a new default cipher list ordering because of the runtime library bump; older agents did not negotiate to a common cipher quickly, resulting in handshake failures.
- A secondary factor: our mux process had a concurrency regression under burst (we're seeing queueing of accept calls and delayed responses).

Immediate mitigation applied at 09:08 PDT: rolled back the mux binary on the affected cohort and temporarily widened the cipher preference list on the control plane to include legacy suites. Errors fell back to baseline within ~6 minutes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Formal rollback postmortem and revert commit for the mux change.
2) Add an explicit preflight test in the pipeline to surface cipher-negotiation mismatches between agent and control plane binaries.
3) Backfill a hotfix that restores graceful accept concurrency behavior.
4) Provide Optima a short lived test build to verify client-side agent negotiation in their environment.

Attaching summary logs and the diagnostic snippet.

—Diego
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary: control plane handshake regressions on us-west private tenant

Hi Anya,

Thank you again for the artifacts and for moving traffic to the fallback region to limit impact. Below is a short incident summary and our action plan. We'll also follow up with a formal postmortem doc and timeline for the code changes.

What happened
- During a staged upgrade of the private control plane (08:30 PDT), a build that included a runtime library bump caused a change in cipher-suite order and introduced a concurrency regression in the mux accept path.
- Result: a subset of your app agents failed TLS negotiation with updated control plane nodes, causing transient handshake failures from ~08:50–09:06 and ~4% error-rate bump in affected services.

What we did
- Identified the root cause and applied a targeted rollback for the mux binary at 09:08.
- Temporarily widened cipher preference list to re-enable negotiation with older agent versions.
- Restored normal traffic patterns by 09:14.

Customer impact
- Short: ~15–20 minutes of elevated app errors for a subset of nodes; Optima reported mitigation by failing over to a fallback region.
- No data exfiltration; no config drift on customer-managed VPCs.

Planned remediation
- Rollback commit will be permanently reverted in the release branch by 2026-07-27 10:00 PDT.
- Pipeline safety: add cross-version cipher-negotiation preflight in CI and an accept-concurrency stress test.
- We will provide a patched control plane image for your validation and a recommended agent update window that preserves rolling compatibility.

Compensation and next steps
- Marissa (cc'd) will propose a 20% credit for the affected hourly Dedicated reservation during the incident window; she'll follow up with details via separate email.
- We will schedule a 30-minute technical review with your platform team on Mon Jul 27 to walk the patch and the validation steps. Proposed time: 10:00–10:30 PDT. Please confirm.

Apologies again for the disruption. We take these incidents seriously and are taking steps to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
